profiles.scope: Strict integer-only canonical JSON bytes, digest format, and cross-language vectors.
limitations: Not the general evaluation-evidence JSON number domain.

profiles.scope: Backend-neutral Effect identity, target, capability, delivery, result, and verification wire object.
limitations: Does not own Host policy, Runtime dispatch, or domain verification.

profiles.scope: Normalized executable Tool interface identity and compatibility classification.
limitations: Provider adaptation and catalog lifecycle remain consumer-local.

profiles.scope: Immutable binding from one Effect to one concrete Tool contract and encoder.
limitations: Binding selection policy and Runtime transport remain outside the protocol.

profiles.scope: Immutable Task, Context, bounded Decision, Dispatch, Observation, Verification, and Outcome wire objects.
limitations: This is a bounded candidate-decision profile, not a universal open-cognition or ActionProposal protocol.
The v1 request-human candidate is a retained compatibility term; future responsibility routing must not assume a human-only receiver.

profiles.scope: Pure reference Effect and Dispatch state algebra plus typed semantic identities.
limitations: Do not expand without a second production consumer; journals, schedulers, and authority roots remain out of scope.

constraintAdmission.protectedFailure: Consumers silently assign different meaning or canonical bytes to the same cross-repository Effect, Binding, Context, Decision, or evidence object.
constraintAdmission.operatingCost: One compact manifest, normative Schemas and vectors, exact consumer pins, and protocol-path compatibility checks per release.
constraintAdmission.deletionTrigger: Delete custom release metadata when a mature package and schema registry binds the same artifacts, consumer compatibility, limitations, and immutable release identity at lower recurring cost.
rejectedAlternatives: independent protocol repository before an independent release cadence

supersessionTrigger: A reproduced cross-consumer failure or materially simpler mature standard requires a new version; v1 objects remain immutable and migrate through explicit vectors rather than silent mutation.
